claude.sample_unit: hospitals (online patient education materials for seven otolaryngology procedures)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of hospital and national organization patient education materials versus NIH sixth-grade standard
links.effect: Nearly all OPEMs exceeded NIH readability standards, averaging 8th-12th grade level across subspecialties; AAO, CSOHNS and ALA materials were harder to read than hospital materials (e.g., AAO 13.3 in head and neck).
links.quote: This study reveals that nearly all otolaryngology OPEMs exceed NIH readability guidelines, creating significant barriers to patient comprehension.

links.outcome: Readability, accuracy, content and tone of ChatGPT-4o generated patient education materials versus hospital and organization materials
links.effect: ChatGPT OPEMs averaged 6.8 grade level, more readable than hospital and organization OPEMs (p ≤ 0.016) with accuracy 4.8-4.9/5; re-prompting for below sixth grade lowered content scores.
links.quote: ChatGPT‐4o generated OPEMs were consistently more readable than both hospital and institutional OPEMs across all specialties ( p ≤ 0.016), except for ENTUK in facial plastics (6.6 vs. 7.2, p = 0.219).

unlisted_practices: Prompting a generative LLM with an explicit target reading level to produce patient education materials, with a trade-off of reduced content completeness

links.outcome: OPEM reading level versus NIH standard
links.effect: Across 144 hospitals, OPEMs averaged 8th-12th grade across subspecialties and exceeded NIH readability standards.
links.quote: Across 144 hospitals, OPEMs exceeded NIH readability standards, averaging at an 8th-12th grade level across subspecialties.

links.effect: Below-sixth prompt produced average readability below sixth grade for all subspecialties except head and neck surgery (6.5-grade level).
links.quote: Upon regeneration of OPEM's with a second prompt specifying readability below the sixth‐grade level, all subspecialty OPEMs, except for head and neck surgery (6.5‐grade level), produced OPEMs at an average readability below the sixth‐grade reading level.
ChatGPT‐generated OPEMs also scored highly for accuracy (4.8/5 to 4.9/5) and patient‐centered tone (4.9/5 for sleep medicine, 5/5 for others).

links.effect: Patient-centered tone was 4.9/5 for sleep medicine and 5/5 for others.
links.quote: ChatGPT‐generated OPEMs also scored highly for accuracy (4.8/5 to 4.9/5) and patient‐centered tone (4.9/5 for sleep medicine, 5/5 for others).

links.outcome: Readability grade level of patient education materials
links.effect: ChatGPT-generated OPEMs averaged a 6.8-grade level across otolaryngology subspecialties, exceeding the NIH sixth-grade readability standard despite prompting to target that level.
links.quote: ChatGPT-generated materials averaged a 6.8-grade level, demonstrating improved readability, especially with specialized prompting, compared to all hospital and organization OPEMs.

unlisted_practices: Prompting generative AI to target a reading level below the desired threshold to achieve target patient readability
